I found one likely bug and one minor lint issue.

1. **`jsonschema/validators.py:278-281`: scope is pushed even when the schema has no id.** `id_of(self.schema)` returns `None` for a schema without `$id`/`id`, and for boolean schemas. `__attrs_post_init__` then calls `push_scope(None)` anyway. `descend` goes through `evolve`, which builds a new validator for every subschema, so each subschema pushes another entry. Nothing pops those entries, because the only `pop_scope` is in `_validate_reference`. The result is a `None` on the `_RefResolver` scope stack. Later `urljoin(resolution_scope, ref)` calls in `resolve` and `resolving` can then fail or resolve against the wrong base. The push needs a guard: `id = id_of(self.schema); if id is not None: push_scope(id)`.

   A related problem is that the scope stack grows on every `descend`, since the pushes are never popped. That can leave a stale base URI in place, so refs inside sibling subschemas may resolve against the wrong base. The new test only has a single root-level `$ref`, so it doesn't exercise this. I'd add a test with nested subschemas that have no `$id`.

2. **`jsonschema/tests/test_validators.py:2397-2398`: three blank lines after the new test.** There are 3 blank lines before `def sorted_errors`, where the style expects 2. flake8 will report E303.

I only read the diff and the surrounding code. I didn't run the tests.
